milestones.text: finished their very first {hobby} project, lopsided and entirely theirs
milestones.post: It's lopsided. It's mine. I'm keeping it.

milestones.text: cleared a corner of their home just for {hobby}
milestones.post: Cleared a corner. It's officially a workspace now.

milestones.text: spent a whole evening on {hobby} and lost all track of time
milestones.post: Looked up and three hours had gone. Good sign?

milestones.text: bought their first proper set of tools for {hobby}
milestones.post: New tools. Very shiny. No idea what half of them do.

milestones.text: had to start their first {hobby} project over three times
milestones.post: Attempt number four. We persist.

milestones.text: asked an experienced neighbour one question about {hobby} and got a whole afternoon of advice
milestones.post: Came for one tip, left with twenty.

milestones.text: gave their first {hobby} attempt to a friend, who was very kind about it
milestones.post: My friend says they love it. My friend is very kind.

milestones.text: learned the names of every basic tool used in {hobby}
milestones.post: I can name every tool on my bench. Using them is next.

milestones.text: made it through a first week of {hobby} without giving up
milestones.post: One week in. Still here.

milestones.text: finished a {hobby} project without needing to undo a single step
milestones.post: Nothing to undo. Who am I.

milestones.text: worked out a mistake on their own instead of starting over
milestones.post: Fixed it myself. Felt like a wizard.

milestones.text: made something with {hobby} that someone actually asked for
milestones.post: Someone requested one. A real request!

milestones.text: kept a steady {hobby} habit going for three months straight
milestones.post: Three months of showing up. Proud of this one.

milestones.text: noticed their hands knew the next step before their head did
milestones.post: My hands are learning faster than I am.

milestones.text: finished a handmade birthday gift with an hour to spare
milestones.post: Made it with an hour to spare. Barely.

milestones.text: started keeping a notebook of {hobby} ideas and measurements
milestones.post: The notebook is filling up fast.

milestones.text: tried a project a level harder than they felt ready for, and finished it
milestones.post: Too hard for me, I said. Finished it anyway.

milestones.text: found their very first attempt in a drawer and laughed at how far they had come
milestones.post: Found my first try. Oh no. Oh, look how far I've come.

milestones.text: had something of their own making mistaken for shop-bought by a stranger
milestones.post: 'Where'd you buy that?' I made it, thank you.

milestones.text: designed a {hobby} project from scratch without following anyone else's plan
milestones.post: My own design. Nobody's instructions but mine.

milestones.text: sold a piece of their own work for the first time
milestones.post: Someone paid real money for a thing I made.

milestones.text: taught a friend the basics of {hobby} over one afternoon
milestones.post: Taught a friend today. Explaining it made me better at it.

milestones.text: finished their most ambitious {hobby} project so far, after weeks of evenings
milestones.post: Weeks of evenings. Worth every one.

milestones.text: got through a whole project without once checking their notes
milestones.post: No notes needed. All from memory.

milestones.text: upgraded to a better set of tools, having finally earned them
milestones.post: Finally got the good tools. I've earned these.

milestones.text: worked out their own shortcut for a fiddly step
milestones.post: Invented a shortcut. Probably not new. Feels new.

milestones.text: filled a whole shelf with things they had made
milestones.post: The shelf is full. Need another shelf.

milestones.text: was asked to teach a small beginners' class in {hobby}
milestones.post: Teaching beginners next week. Nervous and delighted.

milestones.text: entered a piece in the local fair and came home with a ribbon
milestones.post: A ribbon! An actual ribbon!

milestones.text: took on their first paid commission
milestones.post: First commission. Someone trusts me with this.

milestones.text: had a piece put on display for the whole town to see
milestones.post: My work is on display. Trying to act casual.

milestones.text: spent a weekend helping a beginner rescue a project gone wrong
milestones.post: Rescued a beginner's project. Paying it forward.

milestones.text: made a set of six matching pieces, each one as good as the last
milestones.post: Six of them and they all match. Consistency at last.

milestones.text: became the one to ask about {hobby}, the person who knows
milestones.post: Apparently I'm the one people ask now.

milestones.text: finished a piece they would have called impossible a year ago
milestones.post: A year ago this was impossible. Now it's on my table.

milestones.text: sold out of everything they brought to a market stall
milestones.post: Sold out by noon. Went home with an empty basket.

milestones.text: won first prize at a regional show
milestones.post: First prize. Still not over it.

milestones.text: was commissioned for a piece meant to be handed down for generations
milestones.post: Making something meant to outlast me. No pressure.

milestones.text: had a waiting list for their work
milestones.post: There is a waiting list. For my work. Wild.

milestones.text: finished a masterwork that took the better part of a year
milestones.post: Most of a year. It's done. I might weep.

milestones.text: was invited to judge the beginners' section of the local fair
milestones.post: Judging beginners this year. Being very kind about it.

milestones.text: took on an apprentice who wanted to learn {hobby} properly
milestones.post: I have an apprentice. When did that happen?

milestones.text: had a piece chosen as the town's gift to a visiting dignitary
milestones.post: The town gave my piece to a visiting dignitary. Mine!

milestones.text: made a piece their old teacher called better than anything the teacher had made
milestones.post: My old teacher says I've surpassed them. Speechless.

milestones.text: put on a small show of nothing but their own work
milestones.post: A whole show of my work. People came!

milestones.text: got the clay to stay centred on the wheel for a full ten seconds
milestones.post: Ten whole seconds of centred clay. Big day.

milestones.text: made their first bowl, which leans as if listening for something
milestones.post: My first bowl leans. I love it anyway.

milestones.text: pulled up walls that stayed even all the way round
milestones.post: Even walls. The wheel and I are friends now.

milestones.text: trimmed a foot ring neat enough to sign their initials inside
milestones.post: Signed the bottom. It felt official.

milestones.text: glazed a set of four mugs that all came out of the kiln the same colour
milestones.post: Four mugs, one colour. The kiln was kind.

milestones.text: sold their first mug at the studio's holiday sale
milestones.post: A stranger will drink tea from my mug. Thrilled.

milestones.text: threw the tallest vase in the studio that term, in one go
milestones.post: Tallest pot in the studio this term.

milestones.text: knitted their first scarf, which grew steadily wider as it went
milestones.post: My scarf is a trapezoid. It is still a scarf.

milestones.text: learned to cast on without looking at the instructions
milestones.post: Cast on from memory. Small win.

milestones.text: turned the heel of their first sock
milestones.post: Turned a heel. Sorcery.

milestones.text: knitted a pair of mittens that actually match
milestones.post: Two mittens, same size. Unheard of.

milestones.text: finished a cabled sweater that fits
milestones.post: It fits. It actually fits.

milestones.text: knitted a lace shawl fine enough to pass through a ring
milestones.post: Through the ring it went. I'm unbearable now.

milestones.text: won the knitting prize at the county fair with a colourwork blanket
milestones.post: Blue ribbon for the blanket. Still grinning.

milestones.text: crocheted their first granny square, which came out more of a granny circle
milestones.post: It was meant to be a square.

milestones.text: learned to keep their chain stitches all the same size
milestones.post: My chains are even now. Mostly.

milestones.text: stitched forty granny squares together into a whole blanket
milestones.post: Forty squares, one blanket.

milestones.text: crocheted a lace doily fine enough to frame
milestones.post: Framed my doily. Yes, really.

milestones.text: worked out their own pattern for a crocheted collar and wrote it down
milestones.post: My own collar pattern. Keeping it forever.

milestones.text: crocheted a christening gown in fine cotton thread that became a family heirloom
milestones.post: Fine thread, many evenings, one heirloom.

milestones.text: stitched their first initial onto a handkerchief
milestones.post: One letter. Very wobbly. Very proud.

milestones.text: learned to make a French knot that stays put
milestones.post: French knots: conquered.

milestones.text: embroidered a sampler with the whole alphabet on it
milestones.post: A to Z in thread. Done.

milestones.text: stitched a spray of flowers in satin stitch so smooth it shines
milestones.post: Satin stitch that actually shines.

milestones.text: embroidered a cushion cover as a commission for a neighbour
milestones.post: First stitched commission. A cushion!

milestones.text: finished an embroidered wall hanging that took a full year of evenings
milestones.post: A year of stitches. It's on the wall.

milestones.text: sewed a perfectly straight seam on the first try
milestones.post: A straight seam. Who knew.

milestones.text: made their first apron from a single length of cotton
milestones.post: Made an apron. Wearing it to cook.

milestones.text: set in a sleeve without a single pucker
milestones.post: No puckers in the sleeve. Smug.

milestones.text: made a whole shirt from a pattern, buttonholes and all
milestones.post: A full shirt. Buttons and all.

milestones.text: altered a friend's coat until it fit like a made-to-measure one
milestones.post: Took in a coat. It fits like it was made for them.

milestones.text: made a tailored suit from scratch, lining and all
milestones.post: A full suit, lined. My best work yet.

milestones.text: pieced their first quilt block with all the corners meeting
milestones.post: Corners meet! Mostly!

milestones.text: hand-quilted a whole square with tiny, even stitches
milestones.post: Tiny stitches, all the same size.

milestones.text: finished a small quilt for a neighbour's new baby
milestones.post: Small quilt for a small person.

milestones.text: finished a full-size quilt in a star pattern
milestones.post: A whole star quilt. My fingers are tired.

milestones.text: helped run a quilting bee and kept the whole frame moving
milestones.post: Ran the bee. Nobody ran out of thread.

milestones.text: won the quilt prize at the county fair
milestones.post: Best quilt at the fair. Mine!

milestones.text: built their first box, and the lid nearly fits
milestones.post: The lid almost closes. Calling it rustic.

milestones.text: learned to saw along a line instead of somewhere near it
milestones.post: On the line, not near it. Progress.

milestones.text: cut their first dovetail joint that held without glue
milestones.post: A dovetail that holds. Feels like magic.

milestones.text: built a bookshelf that stands level on its own
milestones.post: Level shelves. Every book is safe.

milestones.text: built a rocking chair that rocks evenly
milestones.post: It rocks. In the good way.

milestones.text: built a dining table that seats ten, starting from rough planks
milestones.post: Ten chairs round a table I made.

milestones.text: whittled their first spoon, which holds about one sip
milestones.post: Holds one sip of soup. It's a start.

milestones.text: learned to keep their knife sharp enough to lift clean curls off a pine stick
milestones.post: Sharp knife, clean curls.

milestones.text: carved a little bird that everyone could tell was a bird
milestones.post: People guessed 'bird' first try.

milestones.text: carved a set of four bowls from a single fallen log
milestones.post: One log, four bowls.

milestones.text: carved the painted sign that now hangs over the baker's shop
milestones.post: My sign hangs over the bakery now.

milestones.text: carved a whole set of chess pieces, each with its own face
milestones.post: Thirty-two little faces. Done at last.

milestones.text: stitched their first leather pouch with a proper saddle stitch
milestones.post: Small pouch. Big feelings.

milestones.text: dyed a piece of leather evenly, without a single streak
milestones.post: No streaks. A first.

milestones.text: tooled a pattern of leaves into a belt
milestones.post: My belt has leaves on it now.

milestones.text: made a satchel sturdy enough to carry every day
milestones.post: Carrying a bag I made. Every day.

milestones.text: made a pair of boots that fit
milestones.post: Boots. Made by me. Fit by some miracle.

milestones.text: made a saddle that an old rider praised
milestones.post: Saddle's done. The horse seems to approve too.

milestones.text: made their first pair of earrings from wire and beads
milestones.post: Wearing my own earrings today.

milestones.text: learned to open and close jump rings without bending them out of shape
milestones.post: Jump rings behave now.

milestones.text: soldered a silver ring closed without melting it
milestones.post: Ring soldered. Ring not melted.

milestones.text: set a stone in a bezel that holds tight
milestones.post: Stone set. It's not going anywhere.

milestones.text: sold a whole tray of rings at a craft fair
milestones.post: Empty tray, happy maker.

milestones.text: made a commissioned necklace for a friend's milestone birthday
milestones.post: A necklace for a big birthday. Nervous handover.

milestones.text: painted their first miniature, mostly within the lines
milestones.post: Mostly within the lines. Mostly.

milestones.text: learned to thin their paints instead of using them straight from the pot
milestones.post: Thin your paints, they said. They were right.

milestones.text: painted a tiny face with both eyes looking the same way
milestones.post: Both eyes point the same way. Huge.

milestones.text: finished a whole squad of ten figures in matching colours
milestones.post: Ten little soldiers, all matching.

milestones.text: placed third in the painting contest at the local game shop
milestones.post: Third place! A tiny trophy for tiny art.

milestones.text: won best painted figure at a regional convention
milestones.post: Best in show. For a figure smaller than my thumb.

milestones.text: took apart an old pocket watch and put it back together with only two spare parts
milestones.post: Two parts left over. It still ticks?

milestones.text: learned the name of every wheel in a clock movement
milestones.post: Escapement, pallet, crown wheel. I know words now.

milestones.text: got a stopped mantel clock ticking again
milestones.post: The mantel clock ticks again. Bliss.

milestones.text: built a little clockwork mouse that runs the length of the table
milestones.post: My mouse runs! Startled the cat.

milestones.text: mended a neighbour's music box so it plays the whole tune again
milestones.post: The music box plays again. They teared up.

milestones.text: built a clockwork automaton that pours a cup of tea
milestones.post: It pours tea. It actually pours tea.

milestones.text: wove their first strip of cloth on a small loom, edges wandering
milestones.post: The edges wander. The cloth exists.

milestones.text: learned to warp a loom without tangling the threads
milestones.post: Warped the loom with no tangles.

milestones.text: wove a plain table runner with straight edges
milestones.post: Straight edges at last.

milestones.text: wove a blanket in a twill pattern
milestones.post: Twill! Diagonal lines on purpose!

milestones.text: sold a whole bolt of their cloth at the market
milestones.post: Sold a whole bolt. Proud and a bit sad to see it go.

milestones.text: wove a tapestry showing the village at harvest time
milestones.post: The whole village in thread. Took all winter.

milestones.text: finished a first small project and kept it
milestones.post: Small, wonky, mine.

milestones.text: learned to read a pattern without guessing
milestones.post: The pattern makes sense now.

milestones.text: unpicked a mistake and did it again properly
milestones.post: Undid it. Did it right.

milestones.text: set up a proper corner for tools and materials
milestones.post: My own corner. Everything in reach.

milestones.text: made something small for the house
milestones.post: Made it, using it.

milestones.text: worked out which materials are worth paying more for
milestones.post: Good materials, fewer tears.

milestones.text: learned to keep tools sharp and clean
milestones.post: Sharp, clean, ready.

milestones.text: made a gift that gets used every day
milestones.post: It gets used! Daily!

milestones.text: finished a project in time for a feast day
milestones.post: Ready in time. Barely.

milestones.text: mended something instead of throwing it away
milestones.post: Mended, not replaced.

milestones.text: worked out a technique from watching an old hand
milestones.post: Learned it by watching. Quietly.

milestones.text: made a matching pair on the first attempt
milestones.post: A pair that actually matches.

milestones.text: used up the last of a big bundle of materials
milestones.post: Not a scrap wasted.

milestones.text: finished something useful for the kitchen
milestones.post: Useful. That's the best kind.

milestones.text: was asked to make something for a christening
milestones.post: Made for a christening. Precious.

milestones.text: sold a piece at the market for the first time
milestones.post: Sold at the market. First time.

milestones.text: took on a piece far harder than anything before
milestones.post: Way harder than anything yet. Doing it anyway.

milestones.text: repaired an old family piece so it can be used again
milestones.post: Old piece, new life.

milestones.text: made something for every person at the table
milestones.post: One for everyone. Took weeks.

milestones.text: invented a small trick that saves time
milestones.post: Little trick, big difference.

milestones.text: made a piece with no pattern at all
milestones.post: No pattern. All mine.

milestones.text: was asked to make a piece for the church
milestones.post: For the church. Careful work.

milestones.text: had a piece admired at the fair
milestones.post: Admired at the fair. Glowing.

milestones.text: took orders from three households in one month
milestones.post: Three orders in a month.

milestones.text: taught the basics to a small circle of beginners
milestones.post: Taught a little circle. Loved it.

milestones.text: made a piece fine enough to be kept for best
milestones.post: Too good to use every day.

milestones.text: finished the biggest piece ever attempted
milestones.post: Biggest yet. Done.

milestones.text: won first prize at the harvest fair
milestones.post: First prize. Ribbon and all.

milestones.text: had a piece chosen as a wedding gift for a grand family
milestones.post: A wedding gift for a grand family. My work.

milestones.text: was asked to take on an apprentice
milestones.post: An apprentice. Me, a teacher.

milestones.text: made a piece that will outlast its maker
milestones.post: This one will last longer than me.

milestones.text: was known around town for the quality of their work
milestones.post: Known for it now.

milestones.text: had an old master of the craft ask how a piece was done
milestones.post: The master asked me how. Unreal.

sessions.text: Finished one small part and called it a good evening.
Spent most of the time tidying the workspace, which counts.
Undid an hour's work, then redid it better.
Made steady progress with nothing to show for it yet.
Hummed the whole time without noticing.
Measured twice, then a third time to be sure.
Sorted the scraps into piles that might be useful someday.
Got stuck on one fiddly step and slept on it.
Tried a new technique and liked it more than expected.
Worked by the window to catch the last of the light.
Lost track of time and missed tea.
Started something new before finishing the old thing. Again.
Kept it simple and enjoyed every minute.
Showed the work in progress to a friend, who asked good questions.
Fixed a small mistake nobody else would ever notice.
Laid out everything for tomorrow before stopping.
Took it slow and got it right.
Sketched out a plan for the next project.
